_meta.scope: The street closure and free live music outside the Riverside Theater during Widespread Panic's Oct 23-25, 2026 run, plus the nearby World Series block parties that are NOT part of it.

open_questions: Exact end time of each day's street party is not published. The city closure runs to 11:59 PM nightly and Pabst Theater Group lists only 'Doors Open 12:00 PM' and a 5:30 PM Wolph set; in 2025 the party started at 4:00 PM with music at 5:00 PM. Assume the stage wraps before Riverside doors (6:30 PM) but confirm on site.

Food and drink vendors inside the closed block for 2026 are not published anywhere we could find. Past runs had a beer garden in the street (2017) and Doc's Smokehouse food plus drinks (2021). Molson Coors is Pabst Theater Group's official brewery partner. Expect beer for sale on site; confirm what food is there when you arrive.

Street-party-specific rules (bags, re-entry, chairs, pets, outside drinks) are not published. The bag policy and prohibited-items list on the Wolph page is the Riverside Theater's indoor policy. Milwaukee open-container rules generally apply outside a permitted event footprint, so do not carry drinks out of the closed block.
Pedestrian entrances to the closed block are inferred from the geometry (Plankinton Ave end, Water St end, RiverWalk), not from a published site map.

Stage position is approximate: in past years the stage was set up in Wisconsin Ave in front of the Riverside marquee at Plankinton Ave. Coordinates given are the center of that stretch, not a surveyed point.

After-party prices at Mo's Irish Pub (Houseplant Fri/Sat, Armchair Boogie Sun) are not shown on AXS without starting checkout; they are sold as 21+ add-ons to Widespread Panic tickets. A '3 Day After Party at Mo's Irish Pub' pass is also listed (Fri 11:45 PM start).
MCTS detour notices list the end as 'Sunday, October 25, 2025' (a typo for 2026). Detours almost certainly run through the full closure window.
Deer District's event page shows watch-party hours as 11:00pm-4:00am, which is a time-zone display error (UTC); Radio Milwaukee reports 6-11 PM. We used 6-11 PM.
Yelp photo URL for Mo's Irish Pub could not be verified (Yelp blocks automated requests); left null.
No Houseplant official press photo with a verifiable direct URL was found; used the band's Squarespace profile image (no photographer credit listed).

event.name: Widespread Panic Street Festival (billed by Pabst Theater Group as 'Street Party Before Widespread Panic' with Wolph)
event.organizer: Pabst Theater Group (operator of the Riverside Theater), under a City of Milwaukee special-event street closure permit (Police District 1); Molson Coors is the official brewery partner
event.summary: For the fourth time, the City of Milwaukee is closing West Wisconsin Avenue between North Plankinton Avenue and North Water Street, the block in front of the Riverside Theater that includes the Wisconsin Avenue bridge over the Milwaukee River, from noon Friday through midnight Sunday for Pabst Theater Group's free pre-show street party. Virginia jam band Wolph, whose debut record was produced by Widespread Panic bassist Dave Schools, plays a free outdoor set at 5:30 PM all three days before Panic takes the stage inside at 8:00 PM. The tradition of closing the street and building a beer garden dates to the 2017 run; it is unrelated to the World Series block parties happening the same weekend in the Third Ward and Deer District.
event.cost: Free, no ticket required (Pabst Theater Group: 'FREE SHOWS!')
event.history: Street first closed with a beer garden for the October 20, 2017 run ('For the first time in the history of the fall Widespread Panic runs at the Riverside, the street actually closed down and a beer garden sprouted up'). The city's 2026 notice is labeled '(4TH)'. 2023 street party acts: Steez, Spare Change Trio, Modern Joey (free, from 4 PM). 2025: Round Trip, Magoo, Kyle Hollingsworth (4 PM start, music at 5 PM).

press_mentions.note: 'The long-running jam band takes over Downtown for three nights that include street parties with Wolph before the shows.' Also notes free live audio streams tied to a Hunger Task Force food drive (fans have raised over $45,000 since 2013).
Lists Wolph street party, Houseplant and Armchair Boogie after-parties at Mo's Irish Pub.

closure.streets: W Wisconsin Ave from N Plankinton Ave to N Water St (one block, including the Wisconsin Avenue bridge over the Milwaukee River; the Riverside Theater, 116 W Wisconsin Ave, sits at the west end of this block on the north side)
closure.city_notice_verbatim: WIDESPREAD PANIC STREET FESTIVAL (4TH) (POLICE DISTRICT 1): It is anticipated that from 12:00 P.M. on Friday, October 23 through 11:59 P.M. on Sunday, October 25, 2026 West Wisconsin Avenue between North Plankinton Avenue and North Water Street will be closed to traffic for the "Widespread Panic Street Festival" at the Riverside Theater.
closure.closed_to: All vehicle traffic (pedestrians welcome; this is the festival footprint). MCTS buses detour via W Michigan St.
closure.polygon_note: Corners are the W Wisconsin Ave right-of-way at N Plankinton Ave (west, OSM intersection node 43.038786,-87.911253) and N Water St (east, OSM intersection node 43.038636,-87.909101), offset about 17 m north and south of the centerline. Verified against OpenStreetMap data (api.openstreetmap.org map call, bbox -87.9135,43.0375,-87.9085,43.0405).
entrances: West end: N Plankinton Ave at W Wisconsin Ave, right at the Riverside Theater marquee and Mo's Irish Pub (inferred from geometry)
East end: N Water St at E Wisconsin Ave, east side of the river bridge (inferred from geometry)
Milwaukee RiverWalk stairs/ramps at the west bridge abutment, N RiverWalk Way (inferred from geometry)
closure.cross_river_alternatives_for_cars: W Michigan St bridge (one block south; MCTS detour route) or W Wells St bridge (two blocks north)

rules.rule: Free and open to the public
rules.detail: No ticket needed for the street party; Pabst Theater Group bills it 'FREE SHOWS!' with 'Doors Open 12:00 PM.' Your Widespread Panic ticket is only needed to enter the Riverside (doors 6:30 PM, show 8:00 PM, all ages).

rules.rule: Small purses only inside the Riverside
rules.detail: Only small purses 13" W x 4" D x 9" H or smaller are allowed into the theater, all subject to search. Backpacks and oversized bags are strictly prohibited and there is NO bag storage. Street-party bag rules are not published, but you will be walking straight from the street into the theater, so pack as if the theater rule applies.

rules.rule: No outside food or beverages (including water) into the theater
rules.detail: Prohibited inside: outside food and beverages including water, cans, bottles, alcohol; weapons, laser pens, signs, banners, vapes/e-cigarettes, iPads/tablets, selfie sticks, laptops, pro audio recorders (unless artist-approved), pro photography gear, flash photography. Vape pens are prohibited inside the venues.

Not published for 2026. The closed block has historically been run as a beer garden (2017) with 'drinks to go around' (2023); Molson Coors is PTG's official brewery partner and Sun Cruiser and Jack Daniel's appear as sponsors on the event page. Plan to buy drinks on site rather than bring your own, and do not carry drinks out of the closed block.
All Pabst Theater Group bars and concessions are cashless. Bring a card or phone wallet.
PTG FAQ says you can bring your drink from the venue bar into the theater with you (venue-purchased drinks only).
'Plan to arrive 30 minutes before you want to be in your seat' to clear the security check at the Riverside. With a GA pit, lines form on Wisconsin Ave well before the 6:30 PM doors.

The Houseplant (Fri/Sat) and Armchair Boogie (Sun) after-parties at Mo's Irish Pub and the '3 Day After Party at Mo's Irish Pub' pass are listed '21+ Only' on AXS, sold as add-ons to Widespread Panic tickets. Doors 11:00 PM.

rules.rule: Re-entry, chairs, strollers, pets, smoking outdoors
rules.detail: Not published for the street party. Re-entry is not addressed in the PTG FAQ either. Treat the street as a standing-room festival block; the sidewalks stay open for pass-through.
No published rule. Bublr bike-share docks nearest the theaters are at Cathedral Square and Red Arrow Park (PTG lists these for the Pabst Theater, a few blocks east); Lyft is PTG's rideshare partner.
All PTG venues have accessible entrances, accessible seating and elevators or ramps; email tickets@ptglive.com or call (414) 242-8200 for help. The street party is on flat pavement at street level.

stages.name: Street Party Stage, W Wisconsin Ave at the Riverside Theater
stages.address: W Wisconsin Ave between N Plankinton Ave and N Water St (in front of the Riverside Theater, 116 W Wisconsin Ave), Milwaukee, WI 53203
stages.blurb: The city shuts this one block of Wisconsin Avenue, bridge included, to cars from Friday noon through Sunday night, and Pabst Theater Group turns it into a free outdoor pre-party. Wolph plays at 5:30 PM each day, so you can wander over from the hotel, grab a beer on the pavement, and roll straight into the Riverside when doors open at 6:30 PM.
stages.position_note: Approximate. Exact stage placement within the closed block is not published; historically the setup faced the Riverside marquee near Plankinton Ave.

image.credit: Wolph press photo via Red Light Management

schedule.style: Young Virginia jam band built around two 19-year-old guitarist-singers who started out trading Grateful Dead covers in a garage and grew into a six-piece with two drummers, bass and keys. Their sets are largely improvised, rooted in blues, classic rock and folk, with Dead-songbook covers mixed into originals. Widespread Panic's Dave Schools produced their debut single 'Blue Miracle' and their album 'It's Just Wolph,' so this is very much Panic-family music: loose, groove-first and made for dancing in the street.
schedule.members: Joshua Wright (guitar, vocals), Dylan Stickle (guitar, vocals), Cole Morgan and James Dale (drums), Jacob Spence (bass), Greg Gernon (keyboards)

image.credit: Wolph press photo via Red Light Management (no photographer listed)

schedule.style: Same band all three days. Expect a different, mostly improvised set each night: Dead covers, 'Blue Miracle' and other originals, and long two-drummer jams in the Panic/Dead lineage. If you like the stretched-out second-set feel of a Panic show, this is the warm-up.

image.credit: Wolph press photo via Red Light Management (no photographer listed)

schedule.style: Final free set of the run. Wolph's Dead-leaning, improvisational Southern-rock-meets-psychedelia set is a fitting close before Panic's third night; Red Light Management describes the band as Southern rock with psychedelic sounds and improvisational jamming.

image.credit: Wolph press photo via Red Light Management (no photographer listed)

after_parties.style: Louisville, Kentucky 'genre-fluid' jam band formed in 2020: electric mandolin up front, indie-rock songwriting in the Radiohead/The National vein, and lush psychedelic improvisation, now anchored by former Goose drummer Ben Atkind. Melodic and exploratory rather than bluesy; a good decompression set after Panic.
after_parties.members: Tavis Conley (mandolin, vocals, songwriter), Chris Rodahaffer (guitar), Tommy Arnspiger (bass), Sam Richardson (keys), Ben Atkind (drums, ex-Goose)

after_parties.style: Second of two nights. See Friday.

Madison, Wisconsin jamgrass quartet (banjo, guitar, bass, drums) that plays 'bluegrass at full throttle, infused with the energy of a jam band and the swagger of rock 'n' roll.' Fast picking, funk grooves and a drummer driving everything; think Greensky or Leftover Salmon energy in a packed Irish pub. A hometown-ish favorite for Wisconsin Panic fans.
after_parties.members: Augie Dougherty (banjo, vocals), Ben Majeska (guitar, vocals), Eli Frieders (bass), Denzel Connor (drums)

image.credit: Armchair Boogie via Pabst Theater Group event page

food_and_drink_in_zone.name: Mo's Irish Pub
food_and_drink_in_zone.blurb: The Irish pub literally next door to the Riverside marquee, at the west edge of the closed block. It is the official Widespread Panic after-party bar all three nights (Houseplant Fri/Sat, Armchair Boogie Sun, 21+, doors 11 PM) and the natural indoor fallback if the street gets cold.
food_and_drink_in_zone.zone_note: Sits on the west side of N Plankinton Ave, immediately outside the closed block rather than inside it.

food_and_drink_note: No 2026 vendor list for the closed block was published. Historically the block has hosted a beer garden (2017) and food from Doc's Smokehouse plus drinks (2021). The Riverside's own bars (cashless) open with doors at 6:30 PM.
transit_notes: MCTS CONNECT 1 (Wisconsin Avenue bus rapid transit) detours off Wisconsin Ave between Plankinton Ave and Water St via Michigan St from 12:00 PM Fri Oct 23 through the closure. Wisconsin & Water BRT Station is inactive both directions (stop IDs 9648 eastbound / 9649 westbound). Board eastbound at Wisconsin & N5 (9646) or Wisconsin & Van Buren (9650); westbound at Wisconsin & Jackson (9651) or Wisconsin & N5 (9647). Source: https://www.ridemcts.com/routes-schedules/connect1

MCTS Route 30 (Sherman-Wisconsin) also detours via Michigan St. Inactive stops: Wisconsin & Plankinton (eastbound stop 63, westbound stop 5) and Wisconsin & Water BRT Station (9648/9649). Alternates: eastbound Wisconsin & N3 (62) or Wisconsin & Jackson (66); westbound Wisconsin & Jackson BRT Station (9651) or Wisconsin & MLK/3rd (6). MCTS lists the detour end as 'Sunday, October 25, 2025' (typo for 2026). Source: https://www.ridemcts.com/routes-schedules/30

The Hop streetcar is not affected: no track runs on this stretch of Wisconsin Ave (the M-Line runs east of the river on N Broadway / N Milwaukee St; route map at https://thehopmke.com/interactive-map) and no alerts are posted for Oct 23-25. The Hop is free; hours Fri 5 AM-12 AM, Sat 7 AM-12 AM, Sun 7 AM-10 PM. Sources: https://thehopmke.com/service-updates-alerts and https://thehopmke.com/fares-hours

The Wisconsin Avenue bridge over the Milwaukee River is inside the closure, so cars crossing the river downtown should use the Michigan St bridge (one block south) or Wells St bridge (two blocks north). Source: https://city.milwaukee.gov/dpw/infrastructure/StreetClosures

Pabst Theater Group's discounted parking for the Riverside is the Gimbels Parking Structure, 555 N Plankinton Ave (corner of Plankinton and Michigan; entrances on Plankinton or Michigan, 7 ft 3 in clearance), $11 on weekends, prepaid in advance with show tickets and displayed on the dash; lot opens 2 hours before showtime, good for 6 hours; exit access code 7275. Both entrances are south of the closure and reachable. Source: https://www.pabsttheatergroup.com/parking-riverside

Rideshare: PTG's partner is Lyft but no official pickup zone is published. Wisconsin Ave itself is closed at the theater, so set pickup on W Michigan St or N Plankinton Ave south of Wisconsin, or N Water St east of the bridge. Source: https://www.pabsttheatergroup.com/parking-riverside

Expect heavier-than-usual downtown traffic Friday and Saturday evenings from the Brewers World Series Games 1 and 2 at American Family Field (7 PM) and the Bucks home opener at Fiserv Forum (3 PM Friday), plus the Third Ward and Deer District watch parties. Source: https://radiomilwaukee.org/events-festivals/2026-10-22/brewers-watch-parties-weekend-events

world_series_watch_parties.note: The Wisconsin Avenue closure is a Pabst Theater Group / Widespread Panic event only. The Brewers are hosting the Tampa Bay Rays in World Series Games 1 and 2 (Fri Oct 23 and Sat Oct 24, 7 PM) at American Family Field, and two separate free watch parties, one with its own street closure, are happening within a 15-minute walk.

events.blurb: Fri and Sat, roughly noon to 11 PM: E Menomonee St is closed between N Broadway and N Milwaukee St for a free block party with the games on giant screens at the Third Ward Beer Garden at 7 PM, food trucks, Brewers cocktails, a FOX One 'Relive Live' memorabilia pop-up (noon-4 PM) and free live tapings of the Foul Territory podcast (5-7 PM) with Corey Knebel, Kevin Pillar and Alanna Rizzo. About a 12-minute walk south of the Riverside.
